newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to use $800 mln to pay down debt - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to use $800 mln to pay down debt - CEO.

text.p: Unocal Corp's chief executive officer said on Monday the company would use $800 million from its sale of 76 Products Company to pay down debt, and would consider a stock repurchase with proceeds.

Roger Beach, Unocal's chairman and chief executive officer, said he wanted to "pay down enough debt to receive an A-rating," and lower the company's debt-to-equity ratio to 0.4 percent from 0.46 percent.
Beach spoke during a conference call to reporters.
Tosco agreed to pay $1.4 billion for the fixed assets of 76 Products, including three refineries in California and 1,350 retail stations in the West Coast and Hawaii.

Beach said Unocal, the state's third-largest gasoline retailer, was leaving the cutthroat refining business and would use sale proceeds to invest more heavily in exploration and production in Southeast Asia and Latin America.

"We're getting out of a five percent return on asset business and investing in a much higher return on assets," he said, noting the E&P sector runs a return on asset percentage of 15 to 20 percent The company will focus on a "resource to market" strategy, which includes converting natural gas supplies to power overseas, Beach said.
Unocal would remain headquartered in El Segundo, Calif. "for the present time," Beach said, and would employ 9,400 people.
He declined to speculate if Tosco would lay off any of 76 Products' 3,100 employees and said "there's been no discussion," about the fate of 76 Products president Larry Higby.
He said Tosco, which will have four refineries in California after the sale, "had not indicated at all that they will shut anything down."
Tosco earlier said it secured the company's position as the Number One independent refiner and marketer in the country, with retail fuel sales of 12 million gallons daily.
The deal allows Tosco to use the 76 Products logo and name at retail gasoline stations, Unocal said.
Beach said he did not expect proceeds from the sale to contribute to the 1997 budget.
